topic: Find an equivalent fraction for 1/2 with denominator 8

fullData.title: Finding an Equivalent Fraction on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Fractions

problem.statement: Leo has a pizza cut into 2 equal slices, and he eats 1 slice, which is $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza. He wants to cut the same pizza into 8 equal slices instead. Use the number line to find out how many slices he would need to eat to have the same amount of pizza as $\frac{1}{2}$. Write your answer as a fraction with a denominator of 8.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Count the equal intervals from $0$ to the marked point $\frac{1}{2}$ on the number line to write the fraction in eighths.

steps.title: Count intervals on the number line

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into 8 equal parts with 4 jumps of one-eighth stopping at one-half.

labels.description: Start at zero on the number line.

annotations.steps: I count four equal jumps of one-eighth from zero to reach one-half on the number line.
annotations.strategy: I notice that using a number line helps me see how many eighths fit into one-half by counting the tick marks.
annotations.misconceptions: A common mistake is counting the jump arrows instead of the spaces or tick marks, which leads to an incorrect numerator.
annotations.connections: This connects the visual model of a number line to finding equivalent fractions by scaling the denominator.
annotations.narrative: On the number line, count the tick marks from $0$ to the point $\frac{1}{2}$ at $0.5$: $0.125$, $0.25$, $0.375$, and $0.5$. This equals $4$ intervals, so Leo needs to eat $4$ slices.

challenge.prompt: How many $\frac{1}{8}$ intervals are there on the number line from $0$ to $\frac{1}{2}$?
challenge.rationale: There are 4 intervals of size $\frac{1}{8}$ between $0$ and $\frac{1}{2}$; counting 5 mistakenly counts the tick marks including 0 instead of the spaces.

annotations.steps: Combine 4 parts of size 1/8 to form 4/8, showing the equivalence 1/2 = 4/8.
annotations.strategy: I notice that 4 slices out of 8 equal parts make the exact same amount of pizza as 1 half.
annotations.misconceptions: A common mistake is counting only the slices eaten without realizing the total number of parts increased to 8.
annotations.connections: This shows how equivalent fractions represent the exact same quantity with different denominators.
annotations.narrative: Because the whole pizza from $0$ to $1$ has $8$ equal parts, each slice is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the pizza. Eating $4$ slices gives the equivalent fraction $\frac{4}{8}$.

assignment.prompt: Now that we know Leo needs $4$ one-eighth slices, what is $\frac{1}{2}$ written as an equivalent fraction with a denominator of $8$?
assignment.rationale: Eating 4 slices of size $\frac{1}{8}$ gives the equivalent fraction $\frac{4}{8}$; choosing $\frac{1}{8}$ mistakenly keeps the original single slice without scaling to eighths.
